claim: Researchers can manage shared scenario and turn annotations plus project context labels through engine-free product controls that preserve exact-parent collaborative history.
proved: The selected-scenario product surface exposes whole-scenario or turn-scoped note and flag creation without requiring a model.
Open annotations expose exact-parent edit and resolve controls; resolved annotations expose reopen and do not expose edit until reopened.
Annotation bodies, lifecycle status, last-action attribution, event count, and scenario/turn target are visibly inspectable.
Researchers can create shared project labels, rename them against the displayed current event, and assign or remove them from the selected scenario against the displayed assignment event.
Every product mutation rechecks scenario graph, annotation history, and label history immediately before writing; invalid history is visible and write controls fail closed.
Annotation and label projections advance in deterministic 50-item pages, and assignment lookup is performed only for the visible label page.
The product copy states that notes, flags, labels, and history are shared project data and that installation-provided researcher identity is not authenticated.

The existing domain fixtures still prove 80 reordered or duplicate delivery cases for annotations and labels, exact replay, stale-parent refusal, concurrent branches, disconnected merges, collisions, and orphan detection.
The complete workspace, frontend, structural-audit, production frontend, and native Rust compile gates pass with the new product assets re-embedded.
notProved: A packaged user clicked the annotation or label controls in a webview; product interaction evidence is server-rendered markup plus compiled wiring.
Two physical installations created, edited, resolved, renamed, or assigned the same records through Drive or the LAN bridge.
Researcher identity, display names, timestamps, or ordering clocks are authenticated or trusted.
Moderation, notification delivery, permissions, deletion or retention policy, or branch-reconciliation UI exists.
A project near the 20,000-bucket or 100,000-event bounds remains within a measured memory or interaction-latency budget.
Labels filter the scenario gallery; the current product control manages the selected scenario assignment only.
No live provider, credential, model-quality, policy-text mutation, or network boundary was exercised.
